races.paceDynamic: Quick Quasar is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is expected to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m½f Wolverhampton AW trip. Imola and Hashtagnotions are the principal prominent types likely to track her through the early stages, while the bulk of the field — Silky Lass, Rhythm N Rock, Harbour Vision, Volto Di Medusa and several redistributed hold-up types — will be settled in behind. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than can naturally operate at the rear: Sandret, Ebn Sabt, Molly Valentine and Pipily are all true hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves pushed into an unnatural midfield position simply because there is nowhere further back to go. A single, uncontested pace-setter creating a steady gallop over a distance that favours those who can travel and produce a sustained run from midfield is a race shape that classically suits prominent or well-positioned midfielders who can time their challenge — hold-up horses dropped widest and furthest back face the most ground to make up against a potentially unextended leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quasar Controls, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar leads at a steady tempo and midfield stalkers travel smoothly into contention from two furlongs out
scenarios.body: Quick Quasar's uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop compresses the race in the straight, rewarding horses who have tracked her in the first half of the field; Imola and Rhythm N Rock, both boasting recent course-and-distance form in similar going, are ideally placed to pounce

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves slower than expected and the hold-up horses find a clear run to sustain their finishing effort
scenarios.body: A truly pedestrian gallop collapses the advantage of the leader late and allows progressive finishers like Volto Di Medusa and Silky Lass, both showing recent winning form, to thread through and overhaul

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Quasar Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar is allowed to set a soft, uncontested pace and holds on as rivals fail to close from deep
scenarios.body: An untroubled leader dictating every yard on a Standard surface can simply never be reached if no rival engages early enough; Imola's relentless front-running record makes her the most likely challenger but she may arrive just too late

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race shape produces a ragged, muddled gallop and a lightly-raced or fresh-to-distance runner improves past tired rivals
scenarios.body: A confused early tempo can produce an unusual result, and Pentonville's recent placed form at the distance and Sandret's strong form on Good ground offer each an outside chance if the race falls apart

watchPoints.text: Quick Quasar sets the entire race shape — if she quickens early or is taken on by Imola or Hashtagnotions pushing forward, the pace dynamic changes dramatically and the race could suit deeper hold-up types instead

Sandret and Pipily both return from layoffs of 291 and 318 days respectively — both horses face a significant fitness question on their first runs back, and if either is not fully tuned, they are unlikely to threaten from their enforced midfield positions

Rhythm N Rock carries 156lbs and will be the most closely watched weight-carrier; if his jockey (7lb claim) struggles to place him positively from a hold-up position in a slowly-run race, his finishing effort may be wasted

Imola's trainer Joey Ramsden has only 1 winner from 11 runners over the past 14 days, but Imola herself is in the form of her life with 124211 — any prominent move she makes for position behind Quick Quasar is worth tracking from the outset

races.paceDynamic: Guernsey Angel is the sole confirmed front-runner and will stride into a clear lead from the outset on Wolverhampton's 6f AW straight, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on Standard going that is unlikely to be seriously pressured from the gates. She's Divine is the only other genuine prominent-type and will likely track Guernsey Angel in second, meaning the pace is dictated by just one horse with minimal competition for the lead — a tempo that will almost certainly be steady rather than scorching. The field holds significantly more hold-up and late-running types than can realistically get to the rear: Victor Cee, Tie Fighter, King Of Chaos, Goldenstateofmind, Nzuri, Beach Partee, Filly Foden, and Enter Sandman are all natural hold-up horses competing for the same space, meaning several will be forced wider or closer to the pace than they'd prefer. With a lone leader setting a modest fractions through the early stages and a wall of hold-up runners unable to all get back, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or in the first half of the field without burning petrol, as closers will face a true test of raw finishing speed rather than a collapsing pace to devour.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Guernsey Angel dictates a truly even, unchallenged tempo and the hold-up runners lose ground early on the straight.
scenarios.body: Guernsey Angel bowls along in front setting a measured pace and She's Divine tracks comfortably; closers launch from midfield but the lack of a searching early pace means the leader retains enough in the tank to be brave late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closers Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is marginally stronger than expected and hold-up runners who secure a good position through the first furlong get a clean run.
scenarios.body: Horses with genuine finishing speed that manage to sit midfield — rather than trapped wide or deep — cut down the leader in the final furlong; Enter Sandman and Go Lockers Go, both proven on Standard AW, are best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If She's Divine travels strongly and one of the redistributed hold-up types secures a handy position and the slow pace turns into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace compresses the field and turns the race into a sprint from the two-furlong pole; prominent or just-off-the-pace runners who avoid traffic hold all the advantages and closers find little to close on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners push for positions early and the pace lifts beyond Guernsey Angel's comfort zone in the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Guernsey Angel is headed or pressed hard early, weakens sharply inside the final furlong, and a horse who covered ground efficiently in mid-division swoops late; form horses with demonstrated stamina reserves over 6f on Standard benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Guernsey Angel leads alone at a controlled pace — if Pat Cosgrave is allowed to dictate a slow tempo unchallenged, she may prove very hard to catch late given no horse can close what was never opened up.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses (nine runners sharing the same profile) means significant traffic and interference is likely in the straight — horses drawn wide or caught behind a wall of rivals could see their race over before the furlong pole.

She's Divine is 161 days off the track; if she returns short of peak fitness she could drop away and leave Guernsey Angel with zero cover, hardening the front-runner's chance further than the odds reflect.

Enter Sandman's recent back-to-back wins over this exact course and distance on Standard give him the strongest like-for-like profile in the hold-up group — watch how cleanly George Wood can navigate him through traffic from the two-furlong pole.

Nzuri is flagged as a fader in finishes and will be forced into midfield rather than her natural hold-up position; she is a horse to be against if the market shortens her, as the race shape actively amplifies her main weakness.

races.paceDynamic: With all ten runners carrying a hold-up or rear-racing profile, this 1m4f Wolverhampton handicap has no confirmed front-runner and will be subject to an early tactical vacuum — expect a crawl early before the field compresses and the race ignites in the home straight. The absence of a natural pace-setter means the gallop will almost certainly be slow early, negating stamina advantages and turning this into a flat-out sprint from the turn into the straight. Redistributed hold-up types Last Flight, Ethereal Charm, Keep It Classic, Ada Rose, Risk Averse Rebel, Panthere Noir and Lady Lauren are all genuine rear-runners shown in midfield because the field simply has no leaders; none of them will likely secure any natural prominent position willingly. This race shape strongly favours horses with a sharp turn of foot, decent recent form on Standard AW ground, and the ability to pick up quickly over the final two furlongs — a profile that suits consistent closers like Risk Averse Rebel and horses with upward form trajectories at the right distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no runner takes up the running and the field dawdles for the first mile before a sprint erupts in the straight
scenarios.body: The compressed field will hit the home straight in a bunch and the race becomes a two-furlong dash, eliminating stamina as a factor and rewarding sharp acceleration; horses with recent top-speed figures and AW experience at this track will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one runner or jockey makes a bold move early to establish a proper gallop and strings the field out
scenarios.body: A true-run race over 1m4f will bring stamina into play and expose hold-up horses that lack a staying profile; runners proven at 12f on Standard going will hold an edge in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Nightmare Bunched
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace creates a wall of horses at the turn and several runners face obstruction or a lack of a gap
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses on the inner who cannot find a run will suffer most, while those with room on the wide outside or ridden by experienced handlers will benefit; jockey quality and track positioning in the straight become decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Clear Late
scenarios.trigger: If two horses break from the pack and set up a two-horse duel that the chasing group cannot close down
scenarios.body: The winner would be a horse that reacts first to the injection of pace and sustains it over the remaining distance; early alertness from prominent jockeys like Jack Mitchell or Darragh Keenan could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Risk Averse Rebel has the most consistent placed form in the field at the right trips and on the right surface — if the race develops into a sprint finish Gina Mangan must find a clear run early in the straight.

Keep It Classic is flagged for fading in finishes, which in a slow-pace sprint scenario becomes a major vulnerability — Darragh Keenan will need to time the run perfectly to avoid the horse hitting the wall late.

Mick The Hat is the most recently in form runner with a third just 12 days ago at 12f — watch whether Ralph Beckett's 4/29 T14 barn is firing and whether a switch to Standard suits after the Soft run.
Lady Lauren's form on Soft and Good-to-Soft ground does not translate reliably to Standard AW — Ed de Giles' yard has shown 0/3 in the 14-day window and the surface switch is a genuine unknown.

With no natural front-runner in the field, watch the early stages carefully — the first horse to show any inclination to lead, even briefly, could gain a decisive tactical advantage in a race where the gallop may be almost non-existent for the first mile.

runners_data.name: Sorted

runners_data.name: Thomas Tallis

runners_data.name: Rogue Soldier

races.paceDynamic: Taskheer is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m½f Wolverhampton AW contest and, with no genuine pressing rival to apply heat, is expected to dictate at a sustainable, controlled tempo from the gates. The pace is unlikely to be searching, meaning the early fractions will be modest and the race will almost certainly develop into a steadily-run affair with the field compressed behind Taskheer through the long Wolverhampton bend. This shape hands a significant advantage to closers who can travel economically before producing a late run down the straight, and horses with strong finishing kicks on AW surfaces are the primary beneficiaries. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear; Sorted, Manton Road, Smoker Bellamy, Rogue Soldier, and Thomas Tallis are natural hold-up horses who are likely to be shuffled into a congested midfield rather than finding clear daylight at the back, making race-reading and clear runs late on critically important.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Taskheer Dictates, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Taskheer controls a steady pace unchallenged and the field floods home from midfield-to-rear in the straight.
scenarios.body: Taskheer's uncontested lead sets a falsely slow tempo, compressing the field and making the closing stages a sprint finish; strong AW closers with a proven Wolverhampton record, particularly Arlecchino's Rex and First Encounter, are best positioned to produce a sustained late challenge down the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Compression Creates Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched midfield creates traffic chaos late, rewarding those who find the cleanest passage.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types crammed into midfield, the winner will be the horse whose jockey identifies clear air earliest in the straight; Arlecchino's Rex under Muscutt and First Encounter, both proven multiple AW winners at this course and distance, have the form credentials to benefit from a messy but strongly-run closing furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasting Home
scenarios.trigger: If Taskheer's pace is genuinely economical enough that no closer can reel him in through the short home straight.
scenarios.body: Wolverhampton's tight configuration and the absence of pressing rivals can occasionally allow an unchallenged lead to last longer than expected; Taskheer has twice placed from the front over 8f on this surface and could steal enough of a margin to hold on if the hold-up horses are blocked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Improver Strikes at Big Price
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly-raced or returning horse finds the slow pace perfectly suited and produces a career-best run.
scenarios.body: Rockafeller Skank has won two of her last two starts and, although stepping up significantly in trip on AW for the first time, the slow pace on a flat track could allow her to travel kindly and produce a surprise challenge; Gloriola, freshened after 51 days off, is a secondary candidate if the pace is slow enough to bring her staying power into play.

watchPoints.text: Sorted returns after 84 days off and Rogue Soldier after 145 days — both are significant fitness questions in a race where freshness and peak condition matter given the likely slow pace.

With Sorted, Manton Road, Smoker Bellamy, Rogue Soldier, and Thomas Tallis all forced into a congested midfield, there is a high risk of traffic and interference entering the short Wolverhampton straight — watch for late switches and blocked passages.

Taskheer's ability to control the pace completely unchallenged is the single biggest tactical factor; if anything pressures him early (even accidentally from a slow-starting prominent horse), the race shape changes materially.

Rockafeller Skank's first run on AW after two consecutive soft-ground wins is worth monitoring in the market — if she handles the surface she brings in the best recent form, but the going switch is genuinely unknown.

Arlecchino's Rex and First Encounter share the strongest course-and-distance profiles in the field; watch how their jockeys (Muscutt and Keenan) position them approaching the final turn given the likely midfield traffic.

runners_data.note: The confirmed front runner with form of 2-3 on both Standard AW and Good turf, ridden by the in-form Oisin Orr for the Fahey yard (T14: 8/55); expected to lead unchallenged and set a pace entirely of its own choosing, making this horse the pivotal race-shaper throughout.

runners_data.name: Baby G
runners_data.note: Debutant with no form or going data available; Tony Carroll's yard is busy (T14: 9/52) and Kieren Fox takes the ride — the unknown quantity cuts both ways, but debut runners in maiden sprints over 5f on AW can show natural speed that surprises.

runners_data.name: Good Guys Girl
runners_data.note: Debutant with unknown going profile; Ivan Furtado is a lower-volume trainer (T14: 1/25) and Sean D Bowen is an unusual booking, more associated with jumps, which adds to the uncertainty around this runner's readiness and expected role in the race.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Melody
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true style means it will be last or near last racing from the rear; redistributed to midfield on the map only because the field contains more hold-up runners than the rear can accommodate, but expect Callum Hutchinson to drop in and hunt late — form of 5/6f/Good offers little encouragement on a flat five.

races.paceDynamic: Spaceman is the one confirmed front runner and, with only eight runners over a flat Wolverhampton 5f, is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gate without any serious challenger for the lead. Argy Bhaji will press close enough to keep Spaceman honest, but neither horse is likely to force a truly searching tempo, meaning the fractions should remain manageable rather than punishing. The hold-up brigade — Sheik Yerbouti, Roy Lane, and the true running style of Moonlight Melody — will need the pace to stretch the field in the final two furlongs, but a steady clip on a flat five furlongs rarely delivers that scenario. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Spaceman's controlled fractions and kick at the top of the straight without having covered extra ground; hold-up horses face a stiffer task with no genuine headwind to run into. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, and Moonlight Melody — a genuine hold-up horse — has been redistributed to midfield to reflect that, though Spaceman and Argy Bhaji are best placed to command their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spaceman controls, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Spaceman leads at a fair but not frenetic gallop and the hold-up horses lack the late sprint to close
scenarios.body: Spaceman or Argy Bhaji dictate a rhythm that suits their own finishing effort, and the flat track gives no gradient to naturally string the field out and create the run-in the hold-up types need; the horse tracking the pace most closely arrives with energy in reserve to pounce at the 1f pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutants outrun experience
scenarios.trigger: If one or both of Baby G or Good Guys Girl show natural early pace on debut and inject unexpected pressure into the race
scenarios.body: A sharper tempo than Spaceman wants forces a more genuine test of stamina and speed across the final furlong, levelling the playing field; unexposed types with raw ability can outrun their limited profile evidence if the race becomes a true sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses storm late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sharper than expected and the field strings out through the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Sheik Yerbouti or Roy Lane, given a proper gallop to aim at, can deliver late runs down the outside of a spread-out field; this scenario requires the debutants or Argy Bhaji to push Spaceman beyond its comfort zone in the early stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Project Wallace improves sharply
scenarios.trigger: If Project Wallace, lightly raced and unexposed, produces a significant step forward from its sole start on this surface
scenarios.body: Having already run over 5f on Standard AW going, Project Wallace brings directly relevant form and a Declan Carroll yard in fair current shape; a lightly raced three-year-old with untapped potential can bypass the race shape debate entirely if raw ability is there.

watchPoints.text: Spaceman's early position is the single most important factor — watch whether any debutant (Baby G, Good Guys Girl) jumps quickly and disputes the lead, because that would be the trigger that transforms a controlled scenario into a genuine pace test.

Sheik Yerbouti carries a notable fading-in-finish flag — if this horse does hit the front or produce a sustained challenge, watch whether it gets caught in the final 50 yards as it has done previously.

Roy Lane returns from 53 days off with a tongue tie; a hold-up horse fresh from a lengthy layoff in a race with no anticipated strong gallop is a combination that could leave Pierre-Louis Jamin with no race to run into — watch how the horse travels in the early stages.

Argy Bhaji drops from six furlongs to five for the first time — watch early to see whether the horse travels with the same fluency at the sharper trip or whether it gets outpaced by Spaceman before it can find its stride.

races.name: Cavani Modern Gentleman Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaaranah
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse, shown in midfield on the map only because the race holds far more rear-runners than positions allow; genuine closing style suits a strong pace, which this race may not provide, but excellent Standard Wolverhampton record (2W4P) is compelling and Jack Callan's claim is a practical weight advantage.

runners_data.name: Study Up
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner who will set every yard of pace unopposed; Standard Wolverhampton is fine (7/12), has won over this course and distance at Goodwood, and with no pressure the key question is whether he has enough acceleration to hold on in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Beachborough Girl
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse, redistributed to midfield on the map because of the crowded rear; her excellent Standard record (2W7P in 15 runs) and recent C&D win make her the most credible tracking challenger, and tp headgear suggests she is kept focused.

runners_data.name: Wolf Of Badenoch
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to the redistribution of hold-up runners; Standard Wolverhampton record is poor (0W0P in 4 runs) and the step up from 7-8f distances shown in recent history is a concern over 1m1½f.

runners_data.name: Eagle Day
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up runner with a habit of fading in the finish (flagged); his one AW win came at 8f on Standard and the step up to 1m1½f combined with the fade tendency makes him vulnerable in a slowly-run race where he needs a strong gallop to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose Standard going record is modest (0W2P in 4 runs); primarily a turf performer on Good ground and the AW surface here looks a concern, with no obvious positional advantage in a race dominated by closers.

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with a strong placed record (0W5P in 13 Standard runs) that tells a story of running into placed money rather than winning; steps back from 12f trips, which could be a positive, but Daniel Muscutt will have plenty of company wide in the straight.

runners_data.name: Asian Journey
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse shown in midfield purely due to redistribution; solid Standard record (1W6P in 9 runs) and recent 1W form suggests he is in a decent vein, with Oisin Orr a smart booking for a horse needing to produce a late run.

runners_data.name: Implied Volatility
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse redistributed to midfield; 151 days off the track is a significant fitness flag, Standard record is unremarkable (0W0P in 4), and there is no compelling form case for a first-time-back run over this trip.

runners_data.name: Le Pelerin
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution; form figures of 07-076 and a Standard record of 0W2P in 8 runs suggest he is vulnerable from OR 53, though tp headgear and William Knight's recent 2/14 T14 strike rate provide minor interest.

runners_data.name: Have You A Minute
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 197 days off the track — a major fitness concern; previous form on Standard (2W4P in 12) is decent but a near seven-month break makes it very hard to be confident he will produce his best first time back.

races.paceDynamic: Study Up is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the off, likely settling into a comfortable, uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop over this 1m1½f Wolverhampton AW trip on Standard ground. With no other genuine pace-setter to pressure him, the fractions should be measured and the race is unlikely to truly develop into a test until the home straight. The large hold-up contingent — Eagle Day, Saliko, Pleasant Man, Kaaranah, Asian Journey and others — will have a significant amount of ground to make up off a pace that may not be strong enough to set them alight, meaning finishers could find the winner hard to catch. This race shape strongly favours Study Up and any horse able to track him in a close-up prominent position, as lone front-runners on Standard Wolverhampton going with no pressure frequently hold on; pure hold-up horses are disadvantaged by the lack of early tempo. The field contains far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Kaaranah, Beachborough Girl, Wolf Of Badenoch, Asian Journey, Implied Volatility, Le Pelerin and Have You A Minute are all natural rear-runners who will be competing for the same ground late; of these, Kaaranah and Asian Journey, with their strongest records on this surface and going, are best placed to make their finishing runs count.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Study Up Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Study Up is allowed to bowl along in front at a comfortable clip with no rival willing or able to close the gap until the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Study Up, in receipt of a patient Jonny Peate ride, controls the tempo throughout and uses the final bend to extend his advantage; hold-up horses are left with too much to do off the slow pace and cannot close the deficit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp The Front
scenarios.trigger: If Study Up's pace is slow enough to compress the field, creating a sprint finish that suits the best-weighted hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: With the field bunched entering the straight, Kaaranah and Asian Journey, both proven on Standard Wolverhampton, produce powerful late runs to overhaul a tiring leader; the compressed race effectively neutralises Study Up's positional advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling prominently just behind Study Up — without expending energy to lead — delivers the decisive challenge at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Beachborough Girl, with her strong Standard Wolverhampton form and close-up racing style, is ideally placed to pounce when Study Up begins to weaken; she offers the combination of positional advantage and proven finishing speed on this surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Study Up's fractions are unusually slow and the whole field converges late, creating a lottery that hands an opportunity to lower-rated hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Wolf Of Badenoch or Le Pelerin, both operating off lower handicap marks, could find themselves in the right place at the right time in a muddling finish; their lack of form on Standard going is the key risk factor against this scenario materialising.

watchPoints.text: Study Up — monitor whether Jonny Peate allows the horse to coast in front at a crawl; if the sectionals are very slow, hold-up horses will close rapidly in the straight and the lead advantage could evaporate quickly.

Kaaranah — Jack Callan (3lb claimer) must judge the pace correctly from a hold-up position; if he times the run too late off a slow gallop, the horse's strong Standard record will count for nothing and he will run out of real estate.

Beachborough Girl — Dylan Hogan needs to secure a prominent tracking position early; if she is shuffled back among the cluster of hold-up horses, her natural advantage over this trip and surface is lost in a slow-run race.

Implied Volatility and Have You A Minute — both returning from lengthy layoffs (151 and 197 days respectively); either could show ring-rustiness and should be viewed as likely to need the run before producing their best form.

Wolf Of Badenoch — watch for early positioning by Stevie Donohoe; the horse's poor Standard Wolverhampton record (0W0P) combined with a hold-up style in a slowly-run race makes it very difficult to see how he wins, and market moves would be the only reason to reconsider.
